note: The same shape as Brandon Johnson two days earlier, and the repetition is the point. He passes both physical criteria without argument — a lifelong athlete and former bodybuilding competitor who currently has a six-pack and is training for a HYROX race, asking to get leaner and pain-free, which is good-to-great in its plainest form. He fails all three commercial and situational ones. He is not a business owner or physician but a salesperson eight weeks into a new role selling epoxy, with personal training on the side and a food truck as a future plan. On income the miss is absolute: roughly $400 in his accounts before fuel and food, roughly $400 of monthly surplus, a mid-600s credit score damaged by a consolidation, and one credit card he is actively paying down — against a cheapest instalment of $433 a month. And health is not his neglected area; it is his profession and his identity. Across this batch that pattern now holds for five of the nine sales prospects: fit, motivated, health-literate, and financially outside the offer. The stated ICP has no clinical criterion, which is why a man with five shoulder surgeries reached a closing call unscreened, and its income criterion is not operating as a filter anywhere upstream of the closer.
